newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish court clears old soldier who killed thief.
newsitem.headline: Polish court clears old soldier who killed thief.

text.p: A Polish court cleared a retired army colonel who had shot dead a young man fleeing with a radio stolen from a car, PAP news agency reported on Tuesday.

The court ruled that the 72-year-old colonel, identified only as Wladyslaw H., had not meant to kill Robert S. and had only wanted to prevent a crime when he fired a pistol on a Warsaw street in 1994.
It decided that he had acted out of "necessary defence" in seeking to protect another person's property from a direct attack and pointed to other mitigating factors.
Wladyslaw H. told reporters after the trial that he felt great sympathy for the 22-year-old's bereaved family and would act otherwise if faced with the same situation again, PAP said.
The court said the colonel had tried to persuade the young man to give back the objects he was stealing.
Judge Ewa Grochowska-Szmitkowska stressed that the court's findings should not be applied as a precedent in other situations and no general conclusions should be drawn from it.
The dead man's father and the prosecutor, who had sought a four-year jail sentence for manslaughter, said they would appeal against the verdict.
The case aroused widespread debate and some sympathy for the accused among Poles exasperated after seven years of rising crime since the 1989 fall of communism.
Last May the same court acquitted a woman who had shot at three men stealing copper at night from a transformer by her home, killing one.
Under Polish custom, people involved in legal cases or criminal investigations are not identified by their surnames.
